Couple issues I had with your video. 

1. You need to realize that not a lot of people owned a specific console. The newer console is about to eclipse its *total sales* in the upcoming weeks and isn't even a year old yet. Thus most of these games such as Donkey Kong Country: Tropical Freeze or Bayonetta 2 etc. never got into the hands of many people to begin with, it'll be completely fresh for most. I don't think the company sees this as something they want people to "double dip" on, it's simply there for people who (perhaps rightfully) skipped the older console. I personally own the older console and am not mad about this at all, if anything I'm just happy that more people will get to play some of those amazing games because they deserve more exposure. If I want to buy them a second time over that's on me, I could always go back to the older console and play the game there. 
2. I doubt the company is the only who said "Skyrim on the Switch has to be 60 bucks". Dark Souls Remastered was announced for all platforms just now and is 40 on all of them, including the Switch. So you'll have to take this up with the other developer.  
3. You said that you will never ever support any microtransactions whatsoever for any title from that company. That seems like a rather absolute and harsh stance, dlc/microtransactions are not inherently bad. Mario Kart 8 on the older console was a great example of DLC done right. It brought in a ton of new content including characters and plenty of tracks among multiple cups for a very fair price. DLC is only "bad" because most publishers release bad or overpriced DLC, but it's not a problem with DLC itself.   
After all, all that it means is "downloadable content" - it might very well be the exact same as an expansion pack, the only difference being the ability to download it.
